statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 7 with NQ observed at 29,562.00 in the middle of a two-sided 29,489.75-29,625.50 Globex range and no gap from the 29,538.75 settle; price has retraced about 63 points off the overnight high without extending it, so meaningful retracement remains available. Stress eases slightly to 74 as Brent holds at $99.11 against a 10-year yield of 4.806% and a VIX of 15.72.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-15:00 UTC, the U.S. cash open and first full hour, where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the most plausible route to repeated extension after failed retracements. A secondary checkpoint cluster sits at 17:00 UTC with the 10-year note auction and the Apple keynote. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: NQ retraces to 29,562.00 mid-range with tail at 7, while Brent at $99.11 and a 4.806% 10-year hold stress at 74
body:
As of the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 shows no evidence of mean-reversion failure. NQ futures trade at 29,562.00, up 23.25 points or about 0.08%, inside a Globex range of 29,489.75-29,625.50. That band is 135.75 points, roughly 0.46% wide, and it is two-sided with no gap from the 29,538.75 settle. Over the past hour price has retraced roughly 63 points off the overnight high while leaving that high unextended, which is the direct opposite of the shallow-pullback and failed-retracement structure that would raise tail. Two independent quote sources corroborate the level and the unchanged range. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,681.50 are up 0.01% inside a 15-point range, and the cash Nasdaq-100 closed the prior session at 29,507.70, down 0.12%, so there is a mild cross-index conflict but no directional alignment.

The stress channel remains the cross-asset backdrop rather than the index path. Brent trades at $99.11, up 1.22%, and WTI at $94.17, up 1.23%, both near seven-week highs as the Iran-U.S. exchange of strikes around the Strait of Hormuz continues; U.S. forces disabled or destroyed three Iranian crude tankers on 5 September, including one off Kharg Island, and Iran claimed reciprocal attacks on U.S.-linked vessels. The 10-year yield closed at 4.806%, up 2.2 basis points, near the top of its multi-year range, while the 13-week bill sits at 3.775%. Separately, the administration announced on 8 September a ban on certain Canadian imports covering alcohol, dairy, motorcycles and some autos, effective 29 September, a trade-war escalation whose Nasdaq-100 transmission is indirect. Against all of that the VIX is only 15.72, a benign absolute level that argues the volatility complex is not pricing an imminent disorderly repricing.

The combination gives high stress with low tail: several independent pressures exist, but none has yet produced the persistent directional efficiency in NQ that would deny mean reversion. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was last collected at 01:37 UTC and is beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, so it was used only for headline discovery and each material story was verified against primary reporting; it did not contribute to the price-path assessment.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours the mapped state stayed EA_ON with tail between 5 and 15 and no reading near the block threshold. The single elevated print was 15 at 14:00 UTC on 8 September during a brief trend-down phase in the first full U.S. cash hour, which reverted within the same hour. Stress climbed steadily from 62 to 75 as crude pressed toward $100 on Gulf supply disruption and the 10-year held near the top of its range, while confidence improved from 84 to 89 as live price-path evidence accumulated. One hour, 09:00 UTC on 8 September, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain no Tier-1 U.S. macro release; PPI and jobless claims on 10 September at 12:30 UTC fall just outside the window. Conditional tail stays in a 7-13 band and never approaches the block threshold, peaking across the 13:30-15:00 UTC U.S. cash open where an oil-driven impulse meeting the opening auction is the specific failure mode of concern, with a secondary step at 17:00 UTC for the 10-year note auction and the Apple keynote and a third at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Stress holds in the high band at 73-76 on the crude and long-end backdrop, and confidence decays from 88 to 65 as the observed price path ages across the window.
